clue.text: Excuse bound to have lifted pressure

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting a letter carries it up to the top of the word

parts.note: a bound is a leap
P is the physics abbreviation for pressure

explanation.surface: Someone's excuse is sure to have taken the pressure off them.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'lifted' takes the P of LEAP from the bottom up to the top.
explanation.definitionFit: A plea is a reason offered in defence or mitigation, much like an excuse.

clue.text: Blades surfaced at both sides with oars coming up

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means the whole string is read from bottom to top
the letters at each side of the word surfaced, its first and last

parts.note: oars are rows, the people pulling them in a boat crew

explanation.surface: Rowing blades break the surface on each side of the boat as the oars rise.
explanation.walkthrough: SD, the outsides of 'surfaced', plus ROWS make SDROWS; 'coming up' turns the lot upside down in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Blade is a common poetic word for a sword, so swords are blades.

clue.text: Call for attention having advanced on border

parts.note: A is an abbreviation for advanced, as in A level
a hem is the border of a garment

explanation.surface: A shout for attention from someone who has advanced to the frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: Ahem is the little cough people make to get noticed.

clue.text: Prickly parts of small plants

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
pines are coniferous trees, plants in the wide sense

explanation.surface: A description of the thorny bits on little plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Spines are the sharp prickles on cacti and other plants or animals.

clue.text: Collecting / large screen

definitions.meaning: first meaning: amassing and storing things away
second meaning: a large board for advertising posters, or a fence round a building site

explanation.definitionFit: Hoarding is both the act of stockpiling goods and the British word for a big billboard or temporary fence.

clue.text: Issue register for food parcel

parts.note: to issue is to spring, come out from a source
a roll is an official register of names

explanation.surface: An instruction to put a food parcel on record, like a charity logging donations.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring roll is a Chinese pancake wrapped round a filling, so a parcel of food.

clue.text: Vulgar female dismissed by Nemo, perhaps

indicators.note: the female's letter is sent away from the word, so it is removed

parts.note: Nemo of the film Finding Nemo is a clownfish; 'perhaps' marks him as an example

explanation.surface: A woman is turned away by Nemo, perhaps a submarine captain, as crude.
explanation.walkthrough: Nemo suggests Jules Verne's captain, but it is the cartoon clownfish.
explanation.definitionFit: Clownish behaviour is coarse and boorish, an older sense of vulgar.

clue.text: Mo in second, yet at end clutching bronze

indicators.note: the pair of letters grips the bronze word between them, so it sits inside
only the final letter of yet is taken

parts.note: tan is a bronze colour, as of skin

explanation.surface: A runner called Mo in second place, but holding bronze at the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Mo Farah on the track; Mo here is short for moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A mo is a moment in British slang ('half a mo'), the same as an instant.

clue.text: Walk past bar when on time

parts.note: a prom, short for promenade, is a seafront walk

indicators.note: bar means except, so PAST is taken without the when word

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Stroll past the pub while there is still time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub; it means 'except', so 'past bar when' is PAST minus AS.
explanation.definitionFit: Prompt describes being punctual, arriving at the agreed hour.

clue.text: Sign letter in Greek and French on back

parts.note: tau is the Greek letter T

indicators.note: back means the French word is read the wrong way round

parts.note: sur is French for on

explanation.surface: Describing a lettered sign in Greek and French on the back of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Taurus, the bull, is a sign of the zodiac.

clue.text: Doctor fastening clamping centre of worn raised track

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor

indicators.note: the fastening word holds the centre letters in its grip, so they sit inside it

parts.note: a nail is a fastening

indicators.note: the middle two letters of worn

explanation.surface: A doctor fixing a worn-out piece of equipment by clamping it in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A monorail runs on a single rail, usually elevated above the street.

clue.text: Enjoying being around eastern venture setting up again

indicators.note: the enjoying word surrounds the other pieces, so they go inside it

parts.note: relishing means enjoying
a stab is an attempt, a venture

explanation.surface: Taking pleasure in an eastern business venture being restarted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Enjoying' reads as part of the surface sentence, but it is the outer word; 'venture' means an attempt here, not a business.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-establish is to found or set up something once more.

clue.text: Preacher for one section of church turned up on schedule

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: eg, for example, means for one
the nave is the main body of a church
a list is a schedule

explanation.surface: A preacher arriving at a section of church as the timetable says.
explanation.definitionFit: An evangelist is a travelling preacher who spreads the gospel.

clue.text: Hammered losing first game

indicators.note: the first letter of the drunk word is dropped

parts.note: blotto is slang for very drunk, as is hammered

explanation.surface: A team thrashed after losing the first game of a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hammered' suggests a beaten team, but it means drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotto is a lottery-style game of chance, a version of bingo.

clue.text: Accommodation error picked up

indicators.note: picked up as by a microphone, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a gaffe is a social blunder or error

explanation.surface: A mistake in a booking for lodgings has been spotted.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaff is British slang for one's home or flat, where one lives.

clue.text: Response from pass to defender

parts.note: to feed a player is to pass the ball to them
a back is a defending player in football or rugby

explanation.surface: A footballer's reaction to a pass made to a defender.
explanation.definitionFit: Feedback is a reaction or comments offered in reply to something.

clue.text: Name of hat covering teacher's head

indicators.note: the hat word goes over the head letter, enclosing it

parts.note: tile is old slang for a hat

indicators.note: the head of teacher's is its first letter

explanation.surface: What a hat worn over a teacher's head is called.
explanation.walkthrough: TILE is dated British slang for a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A title is the name of a book, film or piece of music.

clue.text: Central spot mostly dark-coloured part of pan

parts.note: the eye is the central spot, as the eye of a storm or bull's-eye

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, its last letter dropped

parts.note: brown is a dark colour

explanation.surface: A burnt spot in the middle of a frying pan, mostly browned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pan' looks like cookware; it is slang for the face, as in deadpan.
explanation.definitionFit: Pan is slang for a face, and the eyebrow is a feature of the face.

clue.text: Rabbit and ass

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to rabbit is British slang for chatter

explanation.definitionFit: Read as GO ON it means talk at length; read as one word it is a stupid person.

clue.text: European country caught men so suspiciously accepting China's bribe

indicators.note: caught as in heard, so the country's name is taken as it sounds

parts.note: Greece is a European country

indicators.note: the anagrammed letters take the mate word inside them
acting suspiciously, the letters move out of order

parts.note: china is rhyming slang for mate (china plate), so a pal

explanation.surface: A tale of Chinese money being taken in a shady deal by men from a European nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught' is used in the sense of heard, so the country's name counts for its sound; 'China' is not the country but cockney rhyming slang (china plate, mate).
explanation.definitionFit: To grease someone's palm is an idiom for paying them off secretly.

clue.text: Shake a leg alarmed after forgetting Aga cooking foreign bread

indicators.note: alarmed letters are thrown into disorder, a sign to rearrange them
after forgetting means the named letters are left out of the pool
cooking means the oven's letters are mixed up too, removed in any order

parts.note: the letters of 'shake a leg' form the pool
the Aga is a range cooker, whose three letters come out

explanation.surface: A hurry-up urged in alarm after someone forgot the cooker was baking bread.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove A, G, A from SHAKEALEG and rearrange what is left. An Aga is a British range cooker.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread is slang for money, and the shekel is the currency of Israel.

clue.text: Approaches to mask over sadness

indicators.note: the approaches word hides the over letter inside it

parts.note: paths are approaches, ways in
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Ways of hiding one's sorrow behind a mask.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathos is the quality in art or life that stirs pity and sorrow.

clue.text: Unpleasantly wet spades I'm not sure should be put in hall

parts.note: S is the card-suit abbreviation for spades

indicators.note: the doubt sound is placed inside the hall word

parts.note: a lobby is an entrance hall
er is the hesitant noise of someone unsure

explanation.surface: Unsure whether muddy garden spades belong in the hallway.
explanation.definitionFit: Slobbery means covered in drool or slobber, wet in a messy way.

clue.text: Pull sturdy animal bearing north

indicators.note: bearing as in carrying, so the animal holds the north letter inside

parts.note: the yak is a hardy Himalayan ox

explanation.surface: Tugging a strong pack animal northwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To yank is to give a sudden hard tug.

clue.text: On time, vessel proceeds

parts.note: re means on, concerning, as in business letters
an urn is a vessel

explanation.surface: A boat arriving punctually and carrying on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'proceeds' looks like a verb; it is the noun, money made.
explanation.definitionFit: A return is the profit from an investment, the proceeds.

clue.text: Spoke of work and golf

parts.note: to run is to work, operate, as a machine runs
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone talked about their job and golf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoke' looks like the past of speak; it is the noun, a rung of a ladder or crossbar.
explanation.definitionFit: A rung is a crossbar, as a spoke can be on a chair or ladder.

clue.text: Spirit consumed by tipsy chef

indicators.note: the answer is swallowed up inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A spirit drink knocked back by a drunken cook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' suggests alcohol, fitting the tipsy chef; it means the soul.
explanation.definitionFit: The psyche is the human soul or mind, the inner spirit.

clue.text: Recently acquired unowned stray eating fine

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take the fine letter inside them
a stray goes astray, so the letters wander out of order

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A newly adopted stray dog, with no owner, tucking into fine food.
explanation.definitionFit: Newfound describes something only lately discovered or gained.
